articles.title: The East Bay's Indian Food Scene Is Having a Moment — and Diaspora Diners Are Driving It
articles.excerpt: From Sanjeev Kapoor-backed fine dining in Danville to tandoori pizza in Pleasanton and Nepali-Indian fusion in Berkeley, the suburban East Bay has become Northern California's most dynamic corridor for Indian cuisine.
articles.image_caption: An Indian thali spread. The East Bay's Indian restaurant scene has expanded rapidly in 2026, with new openings across San Ramon, Berkeley, and Fremont.
articles.nri_angle: The East Bay's Indian restaurant boom is driven directly by the growing Indian-American population in the suburban Bay Area, with restaurants catering specifically to diaspora dining expectations.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Chia Seed Kheer: A Vegan Janmashtami Dessert That Takes Ten Minutes
articles.excerpt: This no-cook pudding swaps dairy for coconut milk and adds saffron and cardamom for a festive Indian twist on the superfood staple.
articles.image_caption: Chia seed kheer, a quick vegan dessert made with coconut milk and jaggery. The no-cook recipe takes just ten minutes to prepare.
articles.nri_angle: A no-cook vegan dessert that brings traditional Janmashtami flavors to NRI kitchens with ingredients readily available in Western supermarkets.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: New Jersey's Samudhra Restaurant Signs 10,000-Square-Foot Lease for NYC Debut in Hell's Kitchen
articles.excerpt: The Franklin Park Indian restaurant and lounge is bringing its premium dining concept to The Ellery at 312 West 43rd Street, making one of the largest real estate bets by an Indian restaurant in Manhattan.
articles.image_caption: Samudhra, a popular South Indian restaurant in Edison, New Jersey, has signed a lease for a 10,000-square-foot location in Hell's Kitchen to bring its cuisine to Manhattan.
articles.nri_angle: Samudhra's large-format Manhattan bet tests whether Indian cuisine's rising critical and cultural cachet in New York can translate into the commercial scale that other global cuisines achieved long ago
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Biryani By Kilo's Sealed Handi Delivery Takes the Struggle Out of Dum Biryani
articles.excerpt: India's largest dum biryani chain delivers every order in the same earthen pot it's cooked in, complete with a candle-powered reheating kit that ensures the seal-breaking moment is worth the wait.
articles.image_caption: A serving of dum biryani. Biryani By Kilo's sealed-handi delivery model preserves the traditional dum cooking method from kitchen to doorstep.
articles.nri_angle: BBK's sealed handi model taps into deep food memories for NRIs who grew up with communal dum biryani rituals, and has influenced how Indian restaurants worldwide approach biryani presentation
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Masala Vada: The Crispy South Indian Snack That Turns Tea Time Into an Event
articles.excerpt: This chana dal fritter — crunchy outside, crumbly inside — is the definitive tea-time companion across South India. Here's how to make it at home with a step-by-step recipe.
articles.image_caption: Masala vada, a crispy South Indian fritter made from coarsely ground chana dal, onions, and spices. The popular snack is a staple at tea stalls across South India.
articles.nri_angle: For diaspora families missing authentic South Indian snacking culture, masala vada is one of the easiest traditional recipes to recreate at home with widely available ingredients
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Ragi to Kuttu: 5 Healthy Flours for Janmashtami Fasting
articles.excerpt: Nutritionist Dr. Shikha Sharma recommends these traditional Indian flours to make vrat meals nourishing, varied, and lighter than the usual fried fare.
articles.image_caption: Ragi, also known as finger millet, is one of several nutrient-rich flours used in traditional Janmashtami fasting recipes across India.
articles.nri_angle: Diaspora families observing Janmashtami can find kuttu, rajgira, and singhara flours at Indian grocery stores and use these traditional alternatives for healthier fasting meals.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: How To Make Dhaniya Panjiri: A Traditional Janmashtami Recipe
articles.excerpt: This fragrant, no-grain sweet made from roasted coriander seeds, ghee, and dry fruits is the essential bhog offering for Lord Krishna's birthday.
articles.image_caption: Dhaniya panjiri, a traditional no-grain sweet made from roasted coriander seeds, ghee, and nuts. The dish is a staple offering during Janmashtami celebrations.
articles.nri_angle: Indian diaspora families celebrating Janmashtami at home can prepare this traditional prasad with commonly available pantry ingredients.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: How the Avocado Went From 'Butter Fruit' to India's Hottest Ingredient
articles.excerpt: Once an obscure tropical fruit sold for ₹40 a kilo in Mangalore, the avocado has become a fixture on Indian restaurant menus and urban grocery shelves — with a push from the Prime Minister himself.
articles.image_caption: Avocados, long known as butter fruit in South India, have gone mainstream in Indian urban markets and restaurant menus.
articles.nri_angle: For diaspora Indians familiar with avocado culture in the US and Australia, the fruit's rise in India represents a convergence of global food trends and desi culinary innovation — from gilawat kebabs to avocado chaat.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Amul Named World's Strongest Dairy Brand as Indian Food Brands Hit $9.9 Billion
articles.excerpt: Brand Finance's 2026 report ranks Amul first globally for dairy brand strength, with five Indian brands now commanding a combined $9.9 billion in brand value.
articles.image_caption: Amul has been named the world's strongest dairy brand by Brand Finance with a score of 93 out of 100.
articles.nri_angle: Amul's expansion into key US markets brings familiar Indian dairy products closer to diaspora consumers, while the cooperative's global rise underscores the international clout of Indian food brands.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Squash Momo: The Himalayan Dumpling Making Delhi Queue Up at CR Park
articles.excerpt: Limbu Kitchen in Chittaranjan Park has drawn long lines for its iskus momo, a chayote squash-stuffed dumpling rooted in eastern Nepal's culinary traditions.
articles.image_caption: Squash momos at Limbu Kitchen in Delhi's Chittaranjan Park have drawn long queues. The Himalayan dumplings use a seasonal squash filling wrapped in traditional dough.
articles.nri_angle: Chayote squash is widely available at Indian and Hispanic grocery stores in the U.S., making iskus momo an easy Himalayan dish for diaspora cooks to recreate at home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: That Silver Coating on Your Mithai May Be Aluminium, and Doctors Say It Can Harm Your Liver
articles.excerpt: Cheap aluminium foil is increasingly being substituted for genuine silver leaf on Indian sweets, with health experts warning of risks to the liver, kidneys, and nervous system from accumulated heavy metals.
articles.image_caption: Silver-coated Indian sweets. Regulators have found that some silver foil on mithai may actually be aluminium, which doctors warn can harm the liver.
articles.nri_angle: NRIs sending or receiving Indian sweets during festivals should be aware of aluminium-adulteration risks in silver leaf, particularly when buying from unverified sources.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: American Vlogger Tries Kulfi for the First Time in Amritsar, Gives It a Perfect 10
articles.excerpt: Content creator AJ Elizarde discovers India's dense, slow-cooked frozen dessert at a street stall in Punjab and can't stop praising its nutty, milky complexity.
articles.image_caption: Traditional Indian kulfi. An American vlogger gave the frozen dessert a perfect score of 10 after trying it for the first time in Amritsar.
articles.nri_angle: Kulfi reaction videos resonate with diaspora Indians who miss street food experiences that are difficult to replicate abroad, even with store-bought kulfi brands.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Kolkata Goes Beyond Idli-Dosa With Malabari Biryani, Chettinad Chicken and Banana-Leaf Feasts
articles.excerpt: Two major hotel food festivals in the city spotlight lesser-known dishes from Kerala, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu, serving everything from kaima-rice biryani to banana flower fritters.
articles.nri_angle: The broadening of South Indian cuisine beyond idli-dosa in Indian cities mirrors a trend already visible in diaspora restaurants across the Bay Area, London and Toronto.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: How To Make Instant Dosa: The South Indian Classic Without Overnight Fermentation
articles.excerpt: A combination of rice flour, semolina, yogurt and baking soda delivers crisp, golden dosas in under 30 minutes — no soaking or waiting required.
articles.image_caption: A freshly made dosa served on a plate. The South Indian classic can be made without overnight fermentation using an instant batter method.
articles.nri_angle: Instant dosa offers diaspora Indians a practical way to enjoy a South Indian breakfast staple on busy weekday mornings without overnight preparation.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: High-Protein Paneer Tikka: A Gym-Friendly Take on the Classic Indian Starter
articles.excerpt: This tandoori-style paneer tikka delivers up to 25 grams of protein per serving using low-fat paneer, hung curd and minimal oil.
articles.nri_angle: A protein-optimized take on a beloved Indian starter, designed for health-conscious diaspora cooks balancing fitness goals with familiar flavors.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Viral Video of Family Eating on Rajasthan Expressway Sparks Debate, but Context Tells a Different Story
articles.excerpt: A video of a family dining on a newly inaugurated expressway drew outrage, but closer inspection suggests they were at an empty lay-by with no facilities — not trespassing on live traffic lanes.
articles.nri_angle: The viral clip resonated with NRIs who recognize the gap between India's rapid infrastructure expansion and the on-the-ground travel experience their families navigate.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: How To Make Milk Peda: A Classic Indian Sweet With Mathura Roots
articles.excerpt: This simple recipe uses milk powder and condensed milk to recreate the beloved temple sweet in under 30 minutes, no traditional khoya required.
articles.nri_angle: Peda is a staple at Indian sweet shops and festival celebrations across the diaspora, and this home recipe connects kitchens abroad to the Mathura temple tradition.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: How To Make Dhaniya Panjiri for Janmashtami in Under 15 Minutes
articles.excerpt: This traditional coriander-based prasad, made with ghee, dry fruits, and roasted spices, is one of the simplest and most beloved offerings for Lord Krishna's birthday.
articles.image_caption: Dhaniya panjiri, a traditional Janmashtami prasad made with roasted coriander, dry fruits, and sugar.
articles.nri_angle: Panjiri is one of the easiest Janmashtami preparations to replicate abroad, needing only Indian grocery staples.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Elderly Couple's Steel-Plate Paratha Meal on Flight Goes Viral, Reignites Homemade Food Debate
articles.excerpt: A photo of an older couple eating chapatis, sabzi and Amul dahi from a steel thali mid-flight has drawn millions of views and mixed reactions — the latest in a string of viral Indian in-flight food moments.
articles.image_caption: An elderly couple eats homemade chapatis, sabzi and Amul dahi from a steel plate during a flight. The image, posted on X by Nalini Unagar on August 30, has gone viral with millions of views.
articles.nri_angle: The viral moment reflects a deeply Indian travel tradition — packing ghar ka khana for every journey. For the diaspora, the steel thali and Amul dahi packet are instantly recognizable cultural markers, evoking memories of family trips and home-cooked meals that no airline menu can replace.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
